summary: Five-point structural argument on Indian equities: Nifty's 5-yr returns in USD were worse than just holding cash dollars; at PE ~19-20 Nifty looks cheap vs its own history but is at parity with S&P forward PE, so not deeply discounted; earnings quality is the real problem (no Nifty-50 company sustains >20% USD CAGR except possibly Bajaj Finance vs Nvidia at 60% prints); FIIs chase perceived growth which India lacks (no AI/robotics/data-centre plays); and 'curated socialism' (privatise gains, socialise losses) creates political-cycle risk for winners. He took a Nifty swing trade ~24,200 that hasn't worked and will hold for mean reversion to exit. If forced to stay in India: stick to Nifty 50 / high-quality large caps, valuation-aware; still not betting on mid/small caps (promoter dilution). Action plan: diversify internationally (20% to 50% abroad, ETFs fine), hold ~20% gold per 100 equity, only buy cheap valuations and when structural risk is low. Calls: none at ticker level - Nifty, mid/small caps and international markets are all index/category views.
